summary: The construction is valid. Positive packet energy yields a nonzero atomic product-weight measure on the injective parameter lattice; the accepted mixed-integer centerpoint fact supplies an integral center with the required halfspace mass, and strict separation places it in the convex hull of the positive support. Injectivity transfers this center and the weights to distinct positive-volume lattice fibers. The accepted interpolation-depth inequality and metronoid inclusion put the selected affine values in every required fiber metronoid. Affineness then makes the same point belong to every barycentric Minkowski sum, so the complete metronoid core is nonempty, while pullbacks of proper ambient base halfspaces give the required 2^{-n} mass bound, including the whole-preimage case. Zero energy, zero weights, singleton support, q<n, boundary halfspaces, and possible lower-dimensional or empty unselected fibers cause no gap. For the explicit packets, the vertex values depend only on the first interval endpoint, so their canonical interpolation is the displayed affine function; the accepted energy estimate therefore gives the claimed strict lower bound.
